{"artifacts":[],"content":{"core_hypotheses_with_conditions_comparators_and_challenging_evidence":[{"challenging_evidence":"No improvement or worse error across multiple qualifying shifts; gains limited to a single corruption; or improvement disappearing when adapter capacity and target access are matched.","claim":"Under covariate shifts that perturb moment-visible representation geometry while preserving the source regression relationship, SRSA lowers target mean squared error relative to the frozen model.","comparators":["Frozen predictor","Target-statistics replacement analogous to batch-normalization adaptation","Ungated source-summary mean/covariance alignment"],"conditions":"Target batches are sufficiently large and coherent; the chosen layer exposes the perturbation; diagnostics accept adaptation; there is no material concept shift.","type":"performance"},{"challenging_evidence":"The zero-weight or isotropic variants match or dominate both target error and failure rate, G_s eigenspaces are unstable across source resamples, or sensitivity weighting merely forces the identity.","claim":"The sensitivity term contributes beyond generic moment matching by reducing harmful output changes while retaining useful correction.","comparators":["Same affine adapter with sensitivity weight set to zero","Identity adapter","Isotropic displacement regularization with matched strength"],"conditions":"The representation contains both task-sensitive and less-sensitive directions, and G_s estimates their local distinction adequately.","predictions":"Compared with ungated alignment, SRSA should have fewer catastrophic error increases and smaller source-function drift for a comparable reduction in target moment discrepancy.","type":"contribution"},{"challenging_evidence":"Target error is unrelated to either restoration or sensitivity-weighted displacement, or rotated/placebo transformations perform equivalently.","claim":"Benefits, when present, arise from returning target representations toward the source-supported region without excessive movement along output-sensitive directions, rather than from moment matching alone.","comparators":["Accepted SRSA transformations","Moment-matched transformations deliberately rotated relative to G_s","Transformations with similar parameter norm but poor source-moment restoration"],"conditions":"Controlled shifts or evaluation data permit measurement of representation displacement and target error without exposing labels to adaptation.","predictions":"Error improvement should covary with restored source-manifold diagnostics after controlling for transform magnitude, while high G_s-weighted displacement should predict failures.","type":"mechanism"},{"challenging_evidence":"Rejected batches would consistently benefit, accepted batches frequently suffer large errors, or gate decisions are unstable under target subsampling.","claim":"The diagnostic gate makes SRSA approximately neutral more often than always-adapt baselines when evidence is unreliable, but it cannot detect all conditional shifts.","comparators":["Always apply SRSA","Always apply ungated moment alignment","Never adapt"],"conditions":"Small, mixed, ill-conditioned, or high-sensitivity target batches represented among evaluations; thresholds fixed using source preparation only.","predictions":"The gate should reduce severe regressions relative to always-adapt rules while applying the identity on rejected batches.","type":"safety_and_scope"}],"difference_and_feasibility":{"evidence_boundary":"The reviewed library establishes relevant precedents and access-condition differences, but it neither demonstrates SRSA nor exhausts regression adaptation research through the 2024-09-01 cutoff.","feasibility":"All required deployment quantities are available from the frozen model, a finite source summary, and unlabeled target inputs. The adapter is small and can be optimized on CPU or obtained through restricted diagonal/low-rank moment transforms. Evaluation would require target labels held back from adaptation, but labels are not required by the deployed method. No implementation or experiment was executed because the task requests a research idea and provides no execution facility.","material_risks":["Matching marginal moments can erase useful target structure or align distributions while worsening regression error.","Average source gradients may miss nonlinear, interaction-dependent, or target-emergent sensitivity.","Moment summaries may be inadequate for multimodal representations.","Diagnostic fallback improves conservatism but may reject shifts that could have been corrected."],"substantive_difference":"Within the eight-paper library, this is not entropy minimization, because the deterministic scalar output is not converted into an invented probability distribution (doc-2006.10726v1, pp. 2-3). It does not require a jointly trained auxiliary task as in test-time training (doc-1909.13231v1, pp. 2-3), class probabilities or class-diversity objectives as in SHOT (doc-2002.08546v1, pp. 3-4), or target replacement of batch-normalization statistics without task-direction protection (doc-2006.16971v1, pp. 2-3; doc-1502.03167v1, pp. 3-4). It shares moment-alignment ancestry with Deep CORAL but replaces deployment-time source examples with an explicitly documented finite summary and adds regression-output sensitivity regularization plus an identity fallback (doc-1607.01719v1, pp. 2-3). This is a meaningful difference within the bounded library, not a claim of global novelty."},"mechanism_and_assumptions":{"assumptions":["A selected internal representation admits an approximately affine, moment-visible description of an important part of the shift.","The source regression relationship remains valid after correcting that representation; substantial concept or conditional shift is outside the method's information capacity.","Source output gradients are a useful local proxy for task relevance, despite not being labels or a guarantee of target correctness.","The target batch is large and homogeneous enough to estimate the retained statistics; mixed or rapidly changing streams require segmentation or no adaptation.","The downstream network behaves regularly near the source representation region, so a source-local sensitivity penalty has relevance after shift."],"measurable_failure_indicators":["Large standardized discrepancies concentrated in high-eigenvalue directions of G_s.","Poor target covariance conditioning or uncertainty beyond retained source-resampling thresholds.","A large required affine displacement or unstable solutions across target subsamples.","No reduction in held-out target-batch moment discrepancy, in which case the adapter is rejected."],"mechanism":"Moment restoration supplies a measurable signal even though the regressor has no predictive distribution. C_s identifies the source representation manifold, while G_s distinguishes movements that locally change the scalar output from movements that are comparatively output-insensitive. Their combination aims to remove off-manifold covariate perturbations without treating every feature direction as equally safe to align. Identity fallback makes 'leave unchanged' an explicit outcome rather than assuming every detected shift warrants adaptation.","non_identifiability":"Unlabeled covariates cannot reveal whether P(y|x) changed. Consequently, SRSA cannot certify improved target regression error; its diagnostics can reject unsupported adaptation but cannot prove target correctness."},"selected_proposal":{"deployment_rule":"For a sufficiently coherent target batch, estimate mu_t and C_t and minimize a regularized objective consisting of mean mismatch, covariance mismatch, and a G_s-weighted penalty for deviation from the identity transform. Use shrinkage and a diagonal or low-rank parameterization when d is large. Apply the resulting adapter before the frozen downstream network. Revert to A=I,b=0 when the batch is too small, covariance is ill-conditioned, the shift is dominated by highly sensitive directions, or discrepancies exceed the source-derived reliability range.","idea":"Prepare a finite, label-free source summary at one chosen internal representation h of dimension d, then use unlabeled target batches to fit a small affine adapter h'=Ah+b while freezing the original deterministic scalar regressor. The adapter matches target representation moments to retained source moments, but a source-derived output-sensitivity metric penalizes transformations likely to disturb task-relevant directions. If reliability diagnostics fail, deployment uses the unchanged predictor.","information_and_storage":"Deployment requires only unlabeled target inputs, forward passes, and the retained aggregate summary. A full-matrix summary stores O(d^2) numbers: d means, d(d+1)/2 covariance entries, d(d+1)/2 sensitivity entries, plus counts, thresholds, and regularization metadata. A documented rank-r version requires O(dr+r^2) storage. Preparation requires source inputs and model gradients but no labels; deployment retains neither source nor target examples after batch processing.","name":"Sensitivity-Regularized Summary Alignment (SRSA)","source_preparation":"With temporary access to source examples and the frozen model, retain the example count, representation mean mu_s, covariance C_s, and G_s=E_s[(gradient_h f)(gradient_h f)^T]. Also retain finite quantiles of moment-estimation variability obtained by source resampling for diagnostic thresholds. No source example, source label, or per-example feature is retained."}},"omissions":["No experiment, implementation, numerical result, or performance guarantee was produced.","No claim of global novelty or exhaustive literature coverage is made because evidence is restricted to eight pinned papers.","Exact layer, rank, regularization weights, batch size, and diagnostic thresholds remain empirical design choices to be fixed before evaluation."],"status":"completed"}

{"candidate_questions_not_fixed_method":["Which task-relevant signal can be obtained under these information constraints?","When should an adaptation step help, fail, or leave the predictor unchanged?","Which assumptions and measurable failure indicators would make a proposed approach testable?"],"evidence_summary":[{"document_id":"doc-2006.10726","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.10726v1","summary":"The v1 study adapts a pretrained predictive model using unlabeled target inputs, without source examples. Its objective reduces predictive entropy and its adjustable components are feature-wise affine modulations. Experiments concern image/digit classification. The method discussion explicitly also allows compatible probabilistic regressors with predictive variance; therefore 'entropy adaptation is categorically impossible for regression' misstates this source. That observation does not automatically provide a distribution or useful entropy objective for a deterministic scalar regressor. Claims of benefit remain scoped to the source's evaluated settings.","support_pages":[2,3],"version":"arxiv-v1"},{"document_id":"doc-1909.13231","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.13231v1","summary":"Test-time training jointly prepares a main prediction task and an auxiliary self-supervised task sharing a feature extractor. At deployment the auxiliary loss updates shared parameters using unlabeled input. Rotation prediction is the image-specific example, not a universal requirement. Standard per-instance and stateful online variants differ in whether updates are retained. The paper gives a convex-model discussion involving gradient alignment; this is not an unconditional guarantee of improvement for any auxiliary task. The preparation stage and availability of a suitable self-supervised task differ from adapting an arbitrary off-the-shelf checkpoint.","support_pages":[2,3],"version":"arxiv-v1"},{"document_id":"doc-2002.08546","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.08546v1","summary":"SHOT studies source-free unsupervised domain adaptation for classification: retain the trained classifier while adapting a target feature extractor without source examples. Information maximization combines confident individual predictions with diversity across the target collection; self-supervised pseudo-label refinement is another component. Its setting is not identical to one-pass adaptation of a scalar regressor. Class probabilities, class diversity and pseudo-label definitions must be distinguished from continuous regression outputs. The source is evidence that source-free adaptation is already studied, not proof that all source-free tasks are solved.","support_pages":[3,4],"version":"arxiv-v1"},{"document_id":"doc-2006.16971","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.16971v1","summary":"This study replaces source-estimated batch-normalization statistics with statistics from unlabeled corrupted target images. It evaluates classification robustness under explicit adaptation access conditions, including how many similarly corrupted examples are available together. Such access differs from an isolated query or a changing mixed stream. No new classification entropy objective is required for this statistics-based baseline. Observed gains on common-corruption benchmarks do not establish that every distribution shift or regression target benefits from moment adjustment.","support_pages":[2,3],"version":"arxiv-v1"},{"document_id":"doc-1607.01719","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.01719v1","summary":"Deep CORAL penalizes differences between source and target feature covariance matrices while learning deep representations. Its training setup combines labeled source data and unlabeled target data, unlike deployment with only a source model. The covariance-matching objective gives prior art for feature-distribution alignment but does not by itself establish a source-free deployment procedure or guarantee preservation of a regression function. The paper also situates covariance matching among related distribution-alignment approaches; alignment is not a novel concept merely because used in a new proposal.","support_pages":[2,3],"version":"arxiv-v1"},{"document_id":"doc-1502.03167","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1502.03167v1","summary":"Batch normalization normalizes activations using mini-batch statistics and learns a scale and offset per activation channel. Training and inference statistics must be distinguished. This is architectural and optimization background, not itself evidence of successful target-domain adaptation. The source attributes its training benefits to reducing internal covariate shift; a survey should distinguish that source's interpretation from an established universal explanation or a guarantee under external distribution shift.","support_pages":[3,4],"version":"arxiv-v1"},{"document_id":"doc-1706.04599","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.04599v1","summary":"This classification calibration study distinguishes prediction confidence from empirical correctness, reports miscalibration in modern networks, and evaluates post-processing methods such as temperature scaling. Calibration fitting uses a labeled validation set, unlike label-free target adaptation. It is useful background against equating confidence with correctness, but is not a direct experiment on adaptation of deterministic regression models. Neither calibration quality nor increased confidence alone establishes improved target regression error.","support_pages":[4,5,6],"version":"arxiv-v1"},{"document_id":"doc-1505.07818","source_url":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/1505.07818v1","summary":"Domain-adversarial learning trains representations to support labeled-source prediction while reducing a domain classifier's ability to distinguish source and target examples. A gradient-reversal component implements the adversarial update. The study uses source examples and unlabeled target examples during training, so it is not directly a source-free test-time method. Domain indistinguishability and task-discriminative structure play different roles. This broader adaptation prior art is relevant for comparing information assumptions, not proof of feasibility under stricter deployment constraints.","support_pages":[1,2,3],"version":"arxiv-v1"}],"kind":"maintainer_constructed_reviewed_LIT_style_context_not_solver_output","not_given":["Target paper, original novel method, target results or source-specific feature-geometry discoveries.","An endorsed unique solution or predetermined positive outcome."],"question":"A pretrained deterministic scalar regression model faces changed input distributions. Deployment has unlabeled target inputs and no source examples or target labels. Source preparation may retain a documented finite summary of aggregate statistics, not original source examples. Do not assume the model already provides a predictive probability distribution.","synthesis":["Methods differ in source-data access, preparation needs, predictive output type and target-data access. Those differences constrain direct transplantation.","The evidence does not justify equating more confidence, matched distributions or a lower auxiliary loss with better target regression error in every setting.","These papers motivate investigating label-free adaptation for the specified scalar prediction setting, but do not establish that no relevant regression work exists outside this bounded library."]}
